newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates end day unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates end day unchanged.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed unchanged at 19 percent in a trading session marked by speculation and nervousness about the mid-term elections in July, dealers said.
"Near the close rates dropped as some players were demanding paper. However, for most of the day the rates were higher than they were on Tuesday," said one dealer.
Said an analyst, "There was a lot of speculation in the market and rates were up since early in the day due to the upcoming elections which has caused nervousness."
Mexicans will vote on a new Congress, for part of the Senate and for several governors, as well as for a mayor of Mexico City on July 6.
Recent polls show the opposition winning the mayor's job in Mexico City.
The next meeting of the Open Market Committee of the U.S. Federal Reserve is also weighing on market sentiment as investors wonder if U.S. interest rates will rise.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended 90 basis points higher at 20.80 percent.
Liquidity of 1.200 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
